Main.sentence: The United States Armed Forces are the ___E:military forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military)___ of the ___E:United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States)___ .

U.S. ___E:federal law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Code)___ names six armed forces: the ___E:Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army)___ , ___E:Marine Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Marine_Corps)___ , ___E:Navy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy)___ , ___E:Air Force U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Air_Force)___ , ___E:Space Force U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Space_Force)___ , and the ___E:Coast Guard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Coast_Guard)___ .

Since 1949, all of the armed forces, except the Coast Guard, have been permanently part of the ___E:United States Department of Defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Defense)___ , with the Space Force existing as a branch of the Air Force until 2019. They form six of the eight ___E:uniformed services of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uniformed_services_of_the_United_States)___ .

From their inception during the ___E:American Revolutionary War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Revolutionary_War)___ , the Army and the Navy, and later the other services, have played a decisive role in ___E:the country's history U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_United_States)___ .

They helped forge a sense of national unity and identity through victories in the early-19th-century ___E:First U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Barbary_War)___ and ___E:Second Barbary Wars U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Barbary_War)___ .

They played a critical role in the ___E:territorial evolution of the U.S. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territorial_evolution_of_the_United_States)___ , including the ___E:American Civil War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Civil_War)___ .

The ___E:National Security Act of 1947 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Security_Act_of_1947)___ created the Department of Defense or DoD, after a short period being called the National Military Establishment) headed by the ___E:secretary of defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Defense)___ , superior to the service secretaries.
It also created both the U.S.

Air Force and ___E:National Security Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_National_Security_Council)___ ; in 1949, an amendment to the act merged the cabinet-level departments of the Army, Navy, and Air Force into the DoD.
Each of the different military services is assigned a role and domain.
The Army conducts land operations.

The Navy and Marine Corps conduct maritime operations, the Marine Corps specializing in amphibious and maritime littoral operations primarily for supporting the Navy. The Air Force conducts air operations.
The Space Force conducts space operations.
The Coast Guard is unique in that it specializes in maritime operations and is also a ___E:law enforcement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_enforcement_in_the_United_States)___ agency.

The ___E:president of the U.S. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_U.S.)___ is the ___E:commander-in-chief U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commander-in-Chief_of_the_United_States)___ of the armed forces and forms military policy with the DoD and ___E:Department of Homeland Security U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Homeland_Security)___ (DHS), both ___E:federal executive departments U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_federal_executive_departments)___ , acting as the principal organs by which military policy is carried out. The U.S. has used military ___E:conscription U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conscription_in_the_United_States)___ , but not since 1973. The ___E:Selective Service System U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selective_Service_System)___ retains the power to conscript males, requiring the registration of all male citizens and residents of the U.S. between the ages of 18 and 25.

The personnel size of the six armed forces together ranks them among the world's ___E:largest state armed forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_number_of_military_and_paramilitary_personnel)___ .
The U.S.
Armed Forces are widely considered the world's most powerful   and most advanced  military, especially since the end of the ___E:Cold War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War)___ .

The ___E:military expenditure of the U.S. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_budget_of_the_United_States)___ was US$916 billion in 2023, the highest in the world, accounting for ___E:37% of the world's defense expenditures U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_military_expenditures)___ .
The U.S.

Armed Forces has significant capabilities in both defense and ___E:power projection U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_projection)___ due to its large budget, resulting in advanced and powerful technologies which enable widespread deployment of the force globally, including around 800 military bases around the world.
The U.S.
Air Force is the world's largest air force, followed by the ___E:U.S. Army Aviation Branch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army_Aviation_Branch)___ .

The ___E:U.S. Naval Air Forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commander,_Naval_Air_Forces)___ is the fourth-largest air arm in the world and is the largest ___E:naval aviation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_aviation)___ service, while ___E:U.S. Marine Corps Aviation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Marine_Corps_Aviation)___ is the world's seventh-largest air arm. The U.S.
Navy is the world's largest navy by ___E:tonnage U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tonnage)___ .
The U.S.
Coast Guard is the world's 12th-largest maritime force.
The history of the U.S.

Armed Forces dates back to 14 June 1775, with the creation of the ___E:Continental Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_Army)___ , even before the ___E:Declaration of Independence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Declaration_of_Independence)___ marked the establishment of the United States.

The ___E:Continental Navy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_Navy)___ , established on 13 October 1775, and ___E:Continental Marines U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_Marines)___ , established on 10 November 1775, were created in close succession by the ___E:Second Continental Congress U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Continental_Congress)___ in order to defend the new nation against the ___E:British Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire)___ in the ___E:American Revolutionary War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Revolutionary_War)___ .

These forces demobilized in 1784 after the ___E:Treaty of Paris U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Paris_(1783))___ ended the Revolutionary War. The ___E:Congress of the Confederation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_of_the_Confederation)___ created the current ___E:United States Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army)___ on 3 June 1784.  The ___E:United States Congress U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress)___ created the current ___E:United States Navy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy)___ on 27 March 1794 and the current ___E:United States Marine Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Marine_Corps)___ on 11 July 1798.   All three services trace their origins to their respective Continental predecessors.

The 1787 adoption of the ___E:Constitution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Constitution)___ gave ___E:Congress U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress)___ the power to "raise and support armies," to "provide and maintain a navy", and to "make rules for the government and regulation of the land and naval forces", as well as the power to ___E:declare war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Declaration_of_war_by_the_United_States)___ .
The President of the United States is the United States Armed Forces' ___E:commander-in-chief U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commander-in-chief)___ .

The ___E:United States Coast Guard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Coast_Guard)___ traces its origin to the formation of the ___E:Revenue Cutter Service U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revenue_Cutter_Service)___ on 4 August 1790, which merged with the ___E:United States Life-Saving Service U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Life-Saving_Service)___ on 28 January 1915 to establish the Coast Guard.

The ___E:United States Air Force U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Air_Force)___ was established as an independent service on 18 September 1947; it traces its origin to the formation of the ___E:Aeronautical Division, U.S. Signal Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aeronautical_Division,_U.S._Signal_Corps)___ , which was formed 1 August 1907 and was part of the ___E:Army Air Forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army_Air_Forces)___ before being recognized as an independent service in the National Security Act of 1947.

The ___E:United States Public Health Service Commissioned Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Public_Health_Service_Commissioned_Corps)___ was formerly considered to be a branch of the United States Armed Forces from 29 July 1945 until 3 July 1952, and is now one of the eight uniformed services of the United States.
Should it be called into active duty again, it would constitute a seventh branch of the Armed Forces.

The ___E:United States Space Force U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Space_Force)___ was established as an independent service on 20 December 2019. It is the sixth branch of the U.S. military and the first new branch in 72 years.

The origin of the Space Force can be traced back to the ___E:Air Force Space Command U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Force_Space_Command)___ , which was formed 1 September 1982 and was a ___E:major command U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_major_commands_of_the_United_States_Air_Force)___ of the United States Air Force.

Presidential command over the U.S.

Armed Forces is established in ___E:Article II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Article_Two_of_the_United_States_Constitution)___ in the Constitution whereby the president is named as the " ___E:Commander in Chief U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commander-in-Chief_of_the_United_States)___ of the Army and Navy of the United States, and of the Militia of the several States, when called into the actual Service of the United States."

The United States Armed Forces are split between two cabinet departments, with the ___E:Department of Defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Defense)___ serving as the primary cabinet department for military affairs and the ___E:Department of Homeland Security U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Homeland_Security)___ responsible for administering the ___E:United States Coast Guard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Coast_Guard)___ .

The military chain of command flows from the President of the United States to the secretary of defense (for services under the Defense Department) or secretary of homeland security (for services under the Department of Homeland Security), ensuring ___E:civilian control of the military U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civilian_control_of_the_military)___ .

Within the Department of Defense, the military departments ( ___E:Department of the Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_the_Army)___ , ___E:United States Department of the Navy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_the_Navy)___ , and ___E:Department of the Air Force U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_the_Air_Force)___ ) are civilian led entities that oversee the coequal military service branches organized within each department.

The military departments and services are responsible for organizing, training, and equipping forces, with the actual chain of command flowing through the ___E:unified combatant commands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unified_combatant_commands)___ .

The ___E:Joint Chiefs of Staff U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_Chiefs_of_Staff)___ , although outside the operational chain of command, is the senior-most military body of the Department of Defense.

It is led by the ___E:chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chairman_of_the_Joint_Chiefs_of_Staff)___ , who is the military head of the armed forces and principal advisor to the president and secretary of defense on military matters.
Their deputy is the ___E:vice chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_Chairman_of_the_Joint_Chiefs_of_Staff)___ .

Other members include the ___E:chief of staff of the Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_of_Staff_of_the_United_States_Army)___ , ___E:commandant of the Marine Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commandant_of_the_United_States_Marine_Corps)___ , ___E:chief of naval operations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_of_naval_operations)___ , ___E:chief of staff of the Air Force U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_of_Staff_of_the_United_States_Air_Force)___ , ___E:chief of space operations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_of_Space_Operations)___ , and the ___E:chief of the National Guard Bureau U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_of_the_National_Guard_Bureau)___ .

The ___E:commandant of the Coast Guard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commandant_of_the_Coast_Guard)___ is not an official member of the Joint Chiefs, but sometimes attends meetings as one of the military service chiefs.
The ___E:senior enlisted advisor to the chairman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senior_Enlisted_Advisor_to_the_Chairman)___ is the most senior enlisted member in the United States Armed Forces.

The president of the United States, the ___E:secretary of defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Defense)___ , the ___E:secretary of Homeland Security U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Homeland_Security)___ and ___E:chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chairman_of_the_Joint_Chiefs_of_Staff)___ are members of the ___E:United States National Security Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_National_Security_Council)___ , which advises the president on national security, military, and foreign policy matters.

The ___E:national security advisor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Security_Advisor_(United_States))___ , the ___E:homeland security advisor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homeland_Security_Advisor)___ , and the ___E:deputy national security advisor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deputy_National_Security_Advisor_(United_States))___ may also be members of the United States Armed Forces.

The ___E:National Security Council Deputies Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Security_Council_Deputies_Committee)___ also includes the ___E:deputy secretary of defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Deputy_Secretary_of_Defense)___ , ___E:deputy secretary of homeland security U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Deputy_Secretary_of_Homeland_Security)___ , and ___E:vice chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_Chairman_of_the_Joint_Chiefs_of_Staff)___ .

Military leadership, including the secretary of defense, the secretary of Homeland Security, and chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff also sit on the ___E:National Space Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Council)___ .

Unified combatant commands are joint military commands consisting of forces from multiple military departments, with their chain of command flowing from the president, to the secretary of defense, to the commanders of the combatant commands.
Each service organizes, trains, and equips forces that are then presented to the unified combatant commands through service component commands.
Special Operations Command and Cyber Command also present theater special operations commands or joint force headquarters – cyber to other combatant commanders.

Army components are typically dual-hatted as the ___E:joint force land component U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_Force_Land_Component_Commander)___ , Navy components are typically dual-hatted as the ___E:joint force maritime component U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_Force_Maritime_Component_Commander)___ , and Air Force components are typically dual-hatted as the ___E:joint force air component U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_Force_Air_Component_Commander)___ , with the theater special operations command dual-hatted as the joint force special operations component, and Space Force component typically dual-hatted as the joint force space component.

This includes support during conflict or in the conduct of other military activities related to countering threats to U.S. national security.

Rank in the United States Armed Forces is split into three distinct categories: ___E:officers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_(armed_forces))___ , ___E:warrant officers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warrant_officer_(United_States))___ , and ___E:enlisted U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enlisted_rank)___ personnel.

Officers are the leadership of the military, holding commissions from the president of the United States and confirmed to their rank by the ___E:Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate)___ .
Warrant officers hold a warrant from the secretaries of the military departments, serving as specialists in certain military technologies and capabilities.
Upon promotion to chief warrant officer 2, they gain a commission from the president of the United States.
Enlisted personnel constitute the majority of the armed forces, serving as specialists and tactical-level leaders until they become senior non-commissioned officers or senior petty officers.
Military ranks across the services can be compared by U.S.
Uniformed Services pay grade or NATO rank code.
Officers represent the top 18% of the armed forces, serving in leadership and command roles.

Officers are typically commissioned as second lieutenants or ensigns with a bachelor's degree after several years of training and education or ___E:directly commissioned U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Direct_commission_officer)___ from civilian life into a specific specialty, such as a medical professional, lawyer, chaplain, or cyber specialist.

Officers are commissioned through the ___E:United States service academies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_service_academies)___ , ___E:Reserve Officer Training Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reserve_Officer_Training_Corps)___ programs, and the ___E:Officer Candidate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_Candidate_School)___ and ___E:Officer Training Schools U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_Training_School)___ .

During a time of war, officers may be promoted to ___E:five-star ranks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Five-star_rank)___ , with ___E:general of the Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_of_the_Army_(United_States))___ , ___E:fleet admiral U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fleet_admiral_(United_States))___ , and ___E:general of the Air Force U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_of_the_Air_Force)___ the only five-star ranks currently authorized.
___E:Warrant officers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warrant_officer_(United_States))___ are specialists, accounting for only 8% of the officer corps.
Warrant officers hold warrants from their service secretary and are specialists and experts in certain military technologies or capabilities.

The lowest-ranking warrant officers serve under a warrant, but they receive commissions from the president upon promotion to chief warrant officer 2. They derive their authority from the same source as commissioned officers but remain specialists, in contrast to commissioned officers, who are generalists.
There are no warrant officers in the Air Force or Space Force.
Warrant officers are typically non-commissioned officers before being selected, with the exception of Army Aviation where any enlisted grade can apply for a warrant.
Army warrant officers attend the ___E:Army Warrant Officer Candidate School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warrant_Officer_Candidate_School_(United_States_Army))___ .

The rank of ___E:senior enlisted advisor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senior_enlisted_advisor)___ is the highest rank in each service, serving as the primary advisor to its service secretary and service chief on enlisted matters.
Prior to entering service, enlisted personnel must complete their service's ___E:basic training U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recruit_training)___ .

Upon completion of ___E:Marine Corps Recruit Training U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Marine_Corps_Recruit_Training)___ , Infantry Marines attend the ___E:School of Infantry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Marine_Corps_School_of_Infantry)___ .

Non-infantry Marines complete Marine Combat Training before advancing to technical schools for their ___E:Military Occupational Specialty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_Marine_Corps_MOS)___ .

In the Navy, after completing ___E:Recruit Training U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recruit_Training_Command,_Great_Lakes,_Illinois)___ , sailors advance to their "A" schools to complete training for their ___E:rating U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_Navy_ratings)___ .

In the Air Force and Space Force, recruits complete combined ___E:Basic Military Training U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Force_Basic_Military_Training)___ before going to technical training for their ___E:Air Force Specialty Codes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Force_Specialty_Code)___ .

Women such as ___E:Deborah Sampson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deborah_Sampson)___ disguised themselves as men to join the military during the Revolutionary War and War of 1812. Some historians estimate that as many as 400 women disguised themselves as men to enlist during the Civil War. The first woman doctor in the Army, ___E:Mary Edwards Walker U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Edwards_Walker)___ , was commissioned in 1864. In 1901, the ___E:United States Army Nurse Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army_Nurse_Corps)___ was established as a quasi-military auxiliary, followed by the ___E:United States Navy Nurse Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy_Nurse_Corps)___ in 1908.  : 4–9
Women were not accepted in the armed forces outside of medical roles until World War I, when they were allowed to enlist to perform clerical roles.

Women were accepted into the Naval Reserve Force in 1917, and the Marine Corps Reserves and Coast Guard in 1918.  : 9–10 The War Department forbid Army and National Guard posts from employing any women except as nurses,  : 13 but the need for telephone operators overseas during World War I became urgent and hundreds of " ___E:Hello Girls U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hello_Girls)___ " were recruited.
These members of the Army Signal Corps wore military uniforms and took the Army oath, but were classified as civilian employees until 1977 when their military service was officially recognized.

After the ___E:Armistice of 11 November 1918 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armistice_of_11_November_1918)___ was signed, enlisted women were demobilized and the nurse corps returned to peacetime strength.
The Naval Reserve Act of 1916, which authorized the Navy to enlist "citizens", was changed in 1925 to specify "male citizens".  : 16–17
During World War II, all branches of the U.S. military enlisted women.

The ___E:Woman's Army Auxiliary Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women%27s_Army_Corps)___ (WAAC) was established by the Army in 1942 with auxiliary status, and converted to the ___E:Women's Army Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women%27s_Army_Corps)___ (WAC) in June, 1943. [c]  : 24–25 Also formed during this time were the Women's Airforce Service Pilots ( ___E:WASPs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women_Airforce_Service_Pilots)___ ), the Navy's Women Accepted for Volunteer Emergency Services ( ___E:WAVES U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WAVES)___ ), the Marine Corps Women's Reserve, and the Coast Guard Women's Reserve ( ___E:SPARS U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SPARS)___ ).

Women experienced combat as nurses in the ___E:attack on Pearl Harbor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_on_Pearl_Harbor)___ on 7 December 1941, before the U.S. officially entered the war. In 1944, WACs arrived in the Pacific and in Normandy.

During the war, 67 Army nurses and 16 ___E:Navy nurses U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy_Nurse_Corps)___ were captured and spent three years as Japanese prisoners of war. There were 350,000 American women who served during World War II, and 432 were killed in the line of service.
In total, they gained more than 1,500 medals, citations, and commendations.

After World War II, demobilization led to the vast majority of serving women being returned to civilian life. By 1946, the Coast Guard had demobilized all of its women members, while the other branches retained some.  : 105 Law 625, ___E:The Women's Armed Services Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women%27s_Armed_Services_Integration_Act)___ of 1948, was signed by President ___E:Harry S. Truman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_S._Truman)___ , allowing women to serve in the U.S.

Armed Forces in fully integrated units during peace time, albeit with limits that did not apply to men. [d] The intent of Congress was that women should be noncombatants only, but because of the difficulty in defining restrictions for the Army in the law, it was left up to the ___E:service secretaries U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organizational_structure_of_the_United_States_Department_of_Defense#Military_Departments)___ to comply with that intent, although the law did prohibit women from serving aboard ships and on aircraft that engaged in combat missions.  : 118–120 The Army retained a separate corps for women (WAC), while the other services integrated women into their organizational structure.  : 121 In 1951, Executive Order 10240 was issued, authorizing the services to discharge women who became pregnant or had minor children in the home (including stepchildren, foster children, and siblings).  : 125

During the ___E:Korean War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_War)___ of 1950–1953, many women served in the ___E:Mobile Army Surgical Hospitals U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile_Army_Surgical_Hospital)___ .

A recruiting project started in 1951 aimed to increase the number of women in the military from 40,000 to 112,000 by July 1952, but it only achieved 46,000. Some of the reasons were the lack of public support for involvement in Korea; public disapproval of women in the military; fewer women in the right age group due to the low birthrate during the Depression; and the higher standards required for women enlistees.  : 149–155 [e]
In the 1960s, recruiting and training focused on the attractiveness and femininity of women enlistees.

Outside of the medical fields, women were mostly assigned to clerical, administrative, and protocol-related jobs. Women who were previously in technical positions were retrained for the few jobs now permitted for women.

Of the 61 non-combat occupational groups, only 36 were open to women by 1965.  : 180–184 Beginning in 1965, efforts to increase the number of women in the armed forces accompanied concern about the expiration of the Selective Service Act and reduction in enlistment standards to ensure sufficient troops to support the Vietnam War. Public Law 90-130, signed on 8 November 1967, removed the restrictions on female officers in the armed forces and in 1970, two women Army officers were promoted to brigadier general.  : 187–203

During the ___E:Vietnam War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_War)___ , 600 women served in the country as part of the Air Force, alongside 500 members of the WAC and more than 6,000 medical personnel and support staff.  : 205–228
The end of conscription in the early 1970s was a major driver of the expansion of the roles of women in the armed forces.

The number of enlisted and commissioned women in the military hit 110,000 by June 1977.  : 246–250 The ___E:Army Ordnance Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army_Ordnance_Corps)___ began accepting female missile technicians in 1974.  Female crewmembers and officers were accepted into ___E:Field Artillery U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_Artillery_Branch_(United_States))___ missile units.

The services opened up their ___E:Reserve Officers' Training Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reserve_Officers%27_Training_Corps)___ (ROTC) programs to women, and in 1976, women were admitted to the service academies.  : 268–270
In 1974, the first six female naval aviators earned their wings as Navy pilots.

The ___E:Combat Exclusion Policy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Combat_Exclusion_Policy)___ that prohibited women in combat placed limitations on the pilots' advancement,  but at least two retired as captains.
The role of women in the U.S.

Armed Forces received global media attention during the 1991 ___E:Gulf War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_War)___ , though their perception in media was skewed during this time period as little media attention was given to the situations where women faced combat.
In 1991, women were permitted to fly military aircraft.
Since 1994, women have been permitted to serve on U.S. combat ships.
In 2010, the ban on women serving on submarines was lifted.
On 3 December 2015, U.S. defense secretary Ashton Carter announced that all military combat positions would become available to women.

This gave women access to the roughly 10% of military jobs which were previously closed to them.   The various military services were given until January 2016 to provide plans on how they would enforce the policy change.
Many women believed this would allow them to improve their positions in the military, since most high-ranking officers start in combat positions. [citation needed]
